questions.stem: The end products of the complete digestion of protein are

options.text: peptides
amino acids
glucose
fatty acids and glycerol

questions.explanation: Pepsin and trypsin break protein down only as far as peptides; peptidase in the intestinal juice then splits those peptides into individual amino acids, which are small enough to be absorbed. Amino acids are therefore the true end product.

distractorRationale.a: Peptides are intermediates, still too large to be absorbed
distractorRationale.c: Glucose is the end product of carbohydrate digestion
distractorRationale.d: Fatty acids and glycerol are the end products of fat digestion

questions.stem: Which statement about bile is correct?

options.text: It contains lipase, which digests fat into fatty acids and glycerol
It contains no enzymes but emulsifies fat and neutralises stomach acid
It is produced by the pancreas and stored in the liver
It digests protein into amino acids in the duodenum

questions.explanation: Bile is made in the liver, stored in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum. It has two jobs, both physical: its alkaline salts neutralise the acid chyme so that pancreatic enzymes can work, and its bile salts break fat globules into tiny droplets, greatly increasing the surface area for lipase.

distractorRationale.a: Lipase comes from the pancreas and the ileum, not from bile
distractorRationale.c: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder, so both organs are wrong here
distractorRationale.d: Protein is digested by pepsin, trypsin and peptidase, none of which are in bile

questions.stem: Why does the digestion of starch stop temporarily when food reaches the stomach?

options.text: There is no starch left by then
The strongly acidic gastric juice denatures salivary amylase
The stomach has no muscles to mix the food
Starch is absorbed directly through the stomach wall

questions.explanation: Salivary amylase works best in the slightly alkaline conditions of the mouth. Gastric juice brings the pH down to about 2, which changes the shape of the enzyme's active site permanently, so it stops working. Starch digestion only resumes in the duodenum when pancreatic amylase acts in alkaline conditions.

distractorRationale.a: Saliva acts on food for only a short time, so most starch is still undigested
distractorRationale.c: The stomach wall is highly muscular and churns food vigorously
distractorRationale.d: Starch molecules are far too large to be absorbed anywhere in the gut

questions.stem: Which feature of a villus is most directly responsible for the rapid absorption of the products of fat digestion?

options.text: The network of blood capillaries
The central lacteal, a lymph vessel
The layer of goblet cells
The thick muscular wall

questions.explanation: Fatty acids and glycerol are reassembled into fat inside the villus cells and pass into the lacteal, a lymph vessel that eventually empties into the bloodstream near the neck. Glucose and amino acids, by contrast, enter the blood capillaries directly.

distractorRationale.a: Capillaries take up glucose and amino acids rather than the bulk of digested fat
distractorRationale.c: Goblet cells secrete mucus for lubrication; they do not absorb
distractorRationale.d: A villus wall is only one cell thick — a thick wall would slow absorption

questions.stem: Which combination of features best explains why the ileum absorbs digested food so efficiently?

options.text: A thick wall, few villi and a slow blood flow
Numerous villi and microvilli, a wall one cell thick and a rich blood supply
A short length, a muscular wall and abundant mucus
Strongly acidic contents and a large diameter

questions.explanation: Efficient absorption needs a large surface area, a short diffusion distance and a steep concentration gradient. Villi and microvilli supply the area, the single-cell-thick wall supplies the short distance, and continuous blood flow carries absorbed molecules away so the gradient never levels off.

distractorRationale.a: Each of these three features would reduce the rate of absorption
distractorRationale.c: A short gut would reduce contact time, and mucus lubricates rather than absorbs
distractorRationale.d: The ileum is alkaline, and a large diameter reduces rather than increases surface area per volume

questions.stem: The wave-like muscular contraction that moves food along the alimentary canal is called

options.text: peristalsis
emulsification
assimilation
egestion

questions.explanation: Circular muscles contract behind the food and relax in front of it, producing a wave that squeezes the bolus forward. Because the movement is muscular rather than gravitational, swallowing works even when a person is lying down.

distractorRationale.b: Emulsification is the breaking up of fat globules by bile
distractorRationale.c: Assimilation is the use of absorbed food by the body cells
distractorRationale.d: Egestion is the removal of undigested food as faeces

questions.stem: Maltase, secreted in the ileum, acts on

options.text: starch to produce maltose
maltose to produce glucose
protein to produce peptides
fat to produce fatty acids and glycerol

questions.explanation: Enzymes are usually named after the substrate they act on, so maltase acts on maltose. It splits each maltose molecule into two glucose molecules, completing carbohydrate digestion so that absorption can occur.

distractorRationale.a: Starch is converted to maltose by amylase, not maltase
distractorRationale.c: Protein is acted on by pepsin, trypsin and peptidase
distractorRationale.d: Fat is acted on by lipase

questions.stem: Digestion of food is completed in the colon, where the remaining nutrients are absorbed into the blood.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Digestion and nutrient absorption are completed in the ileum. The colon secretes no digestive enzymes; its role is to reabsorb water and mineral salts from the residue before the faeces are stored in the rectum.

questions.stem: A patient has had the gall bladder removed. Which type of food is he most likely to find difficult to digest, and why?

options.text: Starchy food, because amylase is no longer produced
Fatty food, because bile can no longer be stored and released in quantity to emulsify fat
Protein food, because pepsin is no longer secreted
All foods equally, because no enzymes are produced at all

questions.explanation: The gall bladder does not make bile — it stores and concentrates it so a large amount can be released when a fatty meal arrives. Without it, bile trickles continuously from the liver, so large fatty meals are emulsified poorly and lipase works slowly.

distractorRationale.a: Amylase comes from the salivary glands and pancreas, which are unaffected
distractorRationale.c: Pepsin is secreted by the gastric glands in the stomach
distractorRationale.d: All the enzyme-producing organs remain intact; only bile storage is lost

questions.stem: Trace the digestion of a piece of boiled yam from the mouth to absorption, naming the region, the enzyme and the product at each stage. Then state two adaptations of the ileum for absorption.
markingGuide: Mouth: salivary amylase in alkaline saliva converts starch to maltose (2 marks)
Stomach: acidic conditions denature amylase so starch digestion pauses; no carbohydrase acts here (1 mark)
Duodenum: pancreatic amylase converts the remaining starch to maltose in alkaline conditions produced by bile and pancreatic juice (2 marks)
Ileum: maltase converts maltose to glucose, the end product of carbohydrate digestion (2 marks)
Absorption: glucose passes through the villus wall into the blood capillaries by diffusion and active transport, and is carried in the hepatic portal vein to the liver (2 marks)

Two adaptations of the ileum, one mark each: villi and microvilli giving a very large surface area; wall only one cell thick giving a short diffusion distance; dense capillary network maintaining the concentration gradient; great length giving long contact time (2 marks)
questions.explanation: The sequence starch to maltose to glucose must be attached to the correct region and enzyme at each step, including the pause in the stomach caused by the acid denaturing amylase. Adaptations should be paired with the advantage each confers, such as surface area, diffusion distance or maintenance of the gradient.
